strengths: The paper addresses an identifiable question of interest to reinforcement learning, uncertainty estimation, and AI safety researchers: whether cautious behavior can emerge from learned reward uncertainty without explicitly designating safe actions.

The progression from unconditional help to asymmetric action costs, context-dependent help, and sequential driving is well motivated. Comparisons with both single-model optimization and risk-neutral ensemble policies are appropriate for investigating the role of robustness.

The initial help experiment provides encouraging evidence: the strongest robust policy requests help on 89% of fashion images and 68% of letter images in the single-image regime, while retaining high digit accuracy.

The performance-difference-lemma argument provides a useful foundation for extending CFR to continuing MDPs with fixed, known transitions. The main exposition is generally accessible, and the paper explicitly acknowledges limitations involving transition uncertainty, tabular policies, and exact policy evaluation.
weaknesses: Necessary evidence correction: Figures 4 and 21 report incompatible results for the same experiment. With 10% training data in the single-image fashion regime, Figure 4 shows the risk-neutral 10-of-10 policy requesting help approximately 20% of the time, whereas Figure 21 shows approximately 90%. Figures 4 and 22 similarly disagree at 100% training data. This directly affects whether robustness explains the observed caution. The supplied manuscript does not establish which results are correct; this unresolved inconsistency is the main reason for leaning reject.

Necessary mathematical corrections: Appendix B's concentration argument contains reversed probability inequalities in Equations (11) and (13), and Equation (13) has a positive exponent where a negative exponent is required. The martingale argument should explicitly condition on the preceding sampling history. Equation (26) should give a lower bound rather than equality. The intended argument appears repairable, but the printed proof is incorrect.

Necessary claim clarification: Theorem 2 guarantees performance for the best iterate or a uniformly sampled iterate, whereas every experiment evaluates the final iterate after 100 iterations. It does not establish convergence of the final iterate. State this limitation explicitly; the displayed learning curves provide empirical observations, not the missing guarantee.

Necessary interpretation clarification: Figure 5 establishes lower speeds and fewer collisions per discounted time step, but the strongest policy drives very slowly. These statistics do not distinguish improved obstacle avoidance from reduced exposure through driving less. Narrow the collision-avoidance interpretation, or support it with distance traveled, collisions per distance, and a suitable speed-controlled comparison. Discuss the cost of caution on familiar inputs as well: Table 3 reports 84.13% correct classifications for 1-of-20 versus 99.28% for 10-of-10 when help is available.

Necessary reporting clarification: Define the reported uncertainty statistics and distinguish repetitions that shuffle a fixed ensemble from independently retrained ensembles. Explain the architecture-selection criterion and action-dependent loss weighting when asserting an absence of safety-specific tuning. Also reconcile Appendix A's statement that the all-images policy requests help for most letters with the approximately 6% frequency reported in the main text and Figure 8.
Optional improvements: Ensemble-size and uncertainty-diagnostic ablations would help explain when caution emerges and whether the substantial cost of training 2,000 reward models can be reduced.
